svg.title: The overlap state during a WAN migration with two clouds, two defaults and a backdoor link, and the six migration rules
svg.desc: The overlap state shows the legacy hub-and-spoke cloud with its own default route on the left, the new carrier L3VPN cloud with its own default route on the right, and a backdoor link on the far right that becomes a second redistribution point the moment the two clouds are joined. Two consequences follow: two default routes mean administrative distance decides, so failures become inexplicable, and a summary crossing a wave boundary eats the detail routes of un-migrated sites. The working sequence is to inventory backdoors and autonomous system numbers first, build the new cloud beside the old, move sites in waves rather than in one night, verify summarisation at every wave boundary, and decommission the old default last. Six rules follow, each with the trap behind it: phase the migration, inventory backdoors, check PE-CE protocol integration with BGP as the usual choice, decide who generates the default, find every summarisation point, and confirm L2VPN carrier topology. The case lesson is that a media company's Frame Relay to L3VPN move left video loss explained by the old bandwidth and the hub double hop rather than by the new cloud.
svg.text: A WAN migration is a routing design problem, not a circuit swap
During the overlap there are two clouds, two defaults and one backdoor link - and every one of them can become a redistribution point
THE OVERLAP STATE NOBODY DRAWS
legacy hub-spoke cloud
Frame Relay / old MPLS
old default route here
new L3VPN cloud
carrier MPLS VPN
new default route here
backdoor link
branch to branch, or to DC
second redistribution point
migrated sites
Two defaults: administrative distance decides, so failures become inexplicable.
One summary crossing the boundary eats the detail routes of un-migrated sites.
The classic incident: the summary is right on both sides and wrong in between.
SEQUENCE THAT WORKS
1. inventory backdoors and AS numbers first
2. build the new cloud beside the old
3. move sites in waves, not in one night
4. verify summarisation at every wave boundary
5. decommission the old default last
RULE
THE TRAP BEHIND IT
Many branches, many exits: always phase it
one-shot cutover is network-wide risk
Inventory backdoors, IGP areas, AS numbers
a backdoor becomes a second redistribution point
Check PE-CE protocol integration (BGP first)
OSPF as PE-CE constrains areas and LSAs
Decide who generates the default
two defaults let AD decide, unexplainably
Find every summarisation point
summary across a wave boundary is a black hole
For L2VPN confirm the carrier topology
FR hub-spoke to VPLS mesh changes STP entirely
Case lesson: a media company moved Frame Relay to L3VPN with video already on IP - FR bandwidth and the hub double hop, not the new cloud, explained the loss
Migrating transport does not fix a traffic path that was already wrong; measure before you attribute the fault.
